name: ardia
description: A free Chromium browser for the Mac: Arc's sidebar, Dia's polish. Chat on Discord: discord.gg/TdhuXrbcA6

curation.summary: Ardia is a free, open-source Chromium-based browser for macOS (with iOS and Android builds) that reimagines the browser UI by moving the address bar into a sidebar, adding split-view panes, persistent picture-in-picture, built-in uBlock Origin, and Chrome extension compatibility. It positions itself as a fusion of Arc's sidebar-centric design and Dia's polish, with a strong privacy stance (Google pings compiled out, opt-in crash reports).
curation.whyNotable: Ardia is notable for tackling the long-standing problem of browser chrome taking up screen real estate with a genuinely different UI paradigm, while maintaining full Chromium compatibility including extensions and sync. With 100 releases in 6 months, 68 contributors, and multi-platform support (macOS, iOS, Android), it is one of the most actively developed open-source browser projects. Its GPL-3.0 license and privacy-by-default stance (built-in ad/tracker blocking, no telemetry by default) differentiate it in a market dominated by Chromium itself and closed-source alternatives like Arc.
strengths: Genuinely novel browser UI: sidebar address bar, split-view panes, persistent PiP, and toolbar-free design differentiate it from vanilla Chromium and most forks
Exceptional release cadence and project velocity: 100 releases in 6 months, 68 contributors, active Discord community, and multi-platform support (macOS, iOS, Android)
Privacy-first by default: full uBlock Origin built in, Google pings compiled out, opt-in crash reports that exclude site/search data
Full Chrome Web Store compatibility with rebranded 'Add to Ardia' button and cross-device sync, lowering switching friction for users coming from Chrome/Arc
limitations: Fundamentally a Chromium fork: core engine innovation is limited; long-term viability depends on keeping pace with Chromium upstream and Apple's notarization requirements
High complexity and maintenance burden: 854 open issues suggests significant backlog, and browser development is inherently resource-intensive for a small team
Platform risk: Apple's policies on third-party browser engines on iOS and macOS notarization changes could constrain the project's future
useCases: Users who want Arc's sidebar UX but prefer an open-source, privacy-focused, free browser
Power users who multitask with split-view panes and persistent picture-in-picture video
Privacy-conscious users who want built-in ad/tracker blocking and no Google telemetry without configuring extensions manually
curation.targetAudience: macOS (and mobile) power users, privacy-conscious users, and former Arc/Dia users who want an open-source browser with a modern, sidebar-centric UI and full Chrome extension compatibility.
curation.oneLiner: An open-source Chromium browser that moves the address bar into the sidebar, adds split-view panes and persistent PiP, and ships with uBlock Origin and zero Google telemetry — Arc's UX without the lock-in.

name: magpie
description: Pool every plan you pay for — Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, GLM Coding Plan, Kimi Code and more — and use them in any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop… When one runs out, the next takes over.

curation.summary: Magpie is a cross-platform local gateway that lets developers route popular CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.) to any LLM provider through a single unified endpoint. It ships a menu bar/desktop UI for switching models on the fly, with automatic quota tracking and failover across multiple accounts.
curation.whyNotable: It has achieved extraordinary traction (40k+ stars, 163 contributors in ~2 months) by solving a real pain point: coding-agent users being locked into a single model/provider. Its tight integration with major CLI agents plus a polished desktop experience makes it a standout in the AI dev-tooling space.
strengths: Unified local gateway enabling cross-model use of major coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI)
Polished cross-platform desktop/menu-bar UX with quota-aware automatic failover across accounts
Exceptional community momentum: 40k+ stars, 163 contributors, active releases, strong sponsor ecosystem
Well-documented landing page, docs site, reference material, and plugin ecosystem
limitations: No test suite despite production-oriented claims, raising reliability concerns
Very high open-issue count (4,988) relative to project age suggests scaling/maintenance strain
Extremely high release cadence (~100 releases in 6 months) may indicate instability or unpolished changes
Functionally overlaps with existing LLM routers (LiteLLM, one-api), so long-term differentiation depends on agent-specific integrations
useCases: Running Claude Code against alternative models (e.g., Kimi, DeepSeek) without agent-level changes
Centralizing multiple LLM subscriptions/plans behind one interface for cost and quota management
Automatically failing over to backup accounts/providers when rate limits or quotas are hit
curation.targetAudience: Developers who rely on CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) and want freedom to choose or switch underlying LLMs, especially those managing multiple API accounts or subscriptions.
curation.oneLiner: A polished menu-bar LLM gateway that lets any CLI coding agent run on any model, with automatic quota-aware failover across your accounts.

name: davinci-resolve-mcp
description: MCP server integration for DaVinci Resolve Studio

curation.summary: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI assistants (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, etc.) to fully control DaVinci Resolve Studio through its official Scripting API, covering 100% of the API plus guarded workflow helpers. It includes a local browser control panel, an npm-based installer, broad IDE/client configuration, and extensive multilingual documentation.
curation.whyNotable: It brings AI-agent control to one of the most widely used professional video editing, color grading, and audio post-production tools, with unusually comprehensive API coverage (37+ MCP tools, 93.6% live-tested) and a polished installation/management experience for a young project.
strengths: Exceptionally comprehensive DaVinci Resolve Scripting API coverage (100%) with both basic and advanced/offline tool sets
Polished distribution and setup: npm launcher, managed Python venv installer, automatic detection of Resolve paths, and config generation for many MCP clients
Strong engineering maturity for its age: 100 releases in 6 months, CI, tests, 93.6% live-tested coverage, 72 contributors, MIT license
Local browser control panel for inspecting Resolve state, running source-safe analysis, and editing output inline
Multilingual documentation (English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese) and detailed guides/reference
limitations: Tightly dependent on DaVinci Resolve Studio and its scripting API; the free edition requires a special in-app bridge, limiting reach
Niche target domain (professional video/post-production), so value is limited outside that ecosystem
Requires local Python environment and per-client configuration, adding some setup friction despite the installer
useCases: AI-assisted editing, trimming, timeline assembly, and color grading driven by natural language
Automated media pool organization, render queue setup, and project lifecycle tasks
Review marker management, source-safe media analysis, and Fusion/Fairlight operations via an AI assistant
curation.targetAudience: Video editors, colorists, post-production professionals, and creative technologists who want to automate or augment DaVinci Resolve Studio workflows through AI assistants.
curation.oneLiner: A battle-tested MCP server that gives AI assistants full, guarded control over DaVinci Resolve Studio, complete with a local control panel and one-command install.

name: workbuddy2api-panel
description: 把腾讯WorkBuddy账号变成 OpenAI 兼容 API 的多账号网关，同时自动完成任务中心全部任务，附 Web 管理面板（账号池可视化 / 积分任务 / 配置热更新）。基于 Sliverkiss/workbuddy2api 的增强分支

curation.summary: WorkBuddy2API Panel 是一个用 Go 编写的多账号网关，将腾讯 WorkBuddy/CodeBuddy 账号转换为 OpenAI/Anthropic 兼容的 API，并附带 Web 管理面板用于账号池可视化、积分任务自动化和配置热更新。它是已停更上游项目的增强分支，核心功能包括 OAuth 浏览器登录、账号轮转调度、熔断冷却、会话粘性、联网检索以及成长任务一键完成（17/18）。项目明确声明是非官方逆向工程实现，存在账号封禁风险。
curation.whyNotable: 该项目展示了社区在官方 API 缺失时通过逆向工程快速构建兼容层的能力，其多账号池调度、熔断机制和 Web 可视化管理面板的设计具有一定工程参考价值。同时，它反映了围绕 AI 服务灰色地带的生态——大量用户通过非官方渠道获取 OpenAI 兼容接口，也暴露了此类项目的脆弱性（上游随时可能封禁）。维护者对滥用行为的公开警告和对自身精力有限的坦诚披露，使其成为观察开源可持续性困境的一个典型案例。
strengths: 完整的 Web 管理面板，提供账号池可视化、积分任务管理和配置热更新，运维体验优于纯 CLI 工具
成熟的账号池调度机制（轮转、熔断、冷却、会话粘性）源自上游设计，工程细节扎实
活跃维护，发布频繁（6 个月内 100 个 release），有 CI 和 Docker 支持，部署友好
limitations: 本质上是非官方逆向工程实现，依赖对腾讯 WorkBuddy 客户端协议的抓包分析，上游协议变更即可能导致全面失效
无自动化测试，质量保障依赖人工验证；维护者为在读学生，精力有限，响应和更新不可预期
明确存在账号风控/封禁风险，且项目设计天然适合批量小号滥用，已被上游停更归因于此
useCases: 为已有 WorkBuddy/CodeBuddy 账号的用户提供 OpenAI 兼容接口，接入现有 LLM 应用生态
在多账号场景下进行负载均衡和故障转移，最大化利用免费额度
作为研究案例了解 AI 服务逆向工程、账号池调度和 API 网关设计的工程实践
curation.targetAudience: 已拥有腾讯 WorkBuddy/CodeBuddy 账号、希望以 OpenAI 兼容方式接入的开发者；以及对多账号 API 网关和逆向工程技术感兴趣的工程研究者。不适合追求稳定性和合规性的生产环境用户。
comparableProjects: one-api / new-api（通用 AI API 聚合网关）
curation.oneLiner: 一个将腾讯 WorkBuddy 账号转为 OpenAI 兼容 API 的多账号网关，附 Web 面板和任务自动化，但本质是存在封禁风险的非官方逆向工程实现。

name: dsh-our-free-model
description: 在 dsh 里装上这个插件即可，无需登录、注册或填 API Key，就能使用包括 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Kimi K3 在内的前沿模型——完全免费，不限量。 All you do is install this plugin in dsh: no login, no sign-up, no API key — the frontier models are just there, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Kimi K3 among them. Completely free, with no usage cap.

curation.summary: A dsh plugin that provides free, unlimited access to frontier LLMs (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3, GLM 5.3 Flash, MiMo V2.6, etc.) via OpenCode's Zen gateway and Kilo AI's public gateway — no login, registration, or API key required. It's a zero-dependency, no-build-step plugin with model availability probing, reasoning-effort passthrough, hot reload, in-app upgrades, and an OpenAI-compatible local proxy port.
curation.whyNotable: With ~86K stars and trending #1 on GitHub/Trendshift, this plugin has captured massive attention by offering free frontier-model access through existing public gateways, eliminating the usual friction of accounts and API keys. Its transparency about upstream sources and its thoughtful handling of edge cases (content-type mismatch under load, region-limited models, atomic upgrade with rollback) show a level of engineering maturity beyond typical 'free API key' scripts.
strengths: Zero dependencies, no build step — extremely lightweight and easy to audit
Transparent about upstream sources (OpenCode Zen, Kilo AI) with no third-party relay
Robust engineering: SHA-256 verified atomic upgrades with rollback, hot reload, response-shape-based streaming detection, region-limited grouping
Reasoning effort is genuinely propagated as real budget values (reasoning_effort field or token-budget tiers), not just prompt hints
Model list dynamically refreshed from upstream rather than hardcoded; selector only broadcasts routable models
limitations: No tests despite having CI — production confidence is limited
License is NOASSERTION while README badge claims MIT — legal clarity issue
Relies entirely on third-party public gateways whose availability and ToS compliance are outside the project's control
Beta status; upstream gateway changes can break functionality at any time
No Docker or examples directory; onboarding depends heavily on dsh ecosystem familiarity
useCases: Free LLM access for developers who cannot or do not want to pay for API keys
Rapid prototyping and evaluation of frontier models without account provisioning
Local OpenAI-compatible endpoint for tools that expect standard chat-completions APIs
Educational exploration of reasoning-effort controls and model capability differences
curation.targetAudience: Developers already using the dsh (DeepSeek Harness) ecosystem who want free, no-friction access to multiple frontier LLMs; also hobbyists and researchers exploring model behavior across providers.
comparableProjects: free-api-proxy plugins for Claude Code / Cursor
curation.oneLiner: A zero-config dsh plugin that unlocks free, unlimited frontier-LLM access via public gateways — no keys, no accounts, no caps.

Its aggressive quantization strategy and local API compatibility make it a compelling alternative to cloud-dependent solutions.

One-click installation lowers barrier to entry for non-technical users
Broad quantization support maximizes hardware compatibility across low-RAM devices
OpenAI/Anthropic API compatibility enables drop-in replacement for existing tools
Active development cadence with 75 releases and responsive contributor base

Very young project with limited real-world production track record

Drop-in local replacement for OpenAI/Anthropic APIs in development workflows
Running capable coding assistants on laptops and workstations with constrained VRAM
On-premise AI deployment for organizations with data residency requirements

name: nod

curation.summary: Nod is an open-source, local-first personal AI agent built by n8n that runs on your machine and autonomously performs real-world web tasks — such as chasing invoices, prepping calls, and cancelling trials — while asking for confirmation before acting. It supports multiple LLM providers (ChatGPT Plus/Pro or custom AI keys) and includes desktop apps for macOS, Windows, and Linux preview. Positioned as a privacy-focused alternative to cloud-only assistants, it integrates with messaging platforms like Telegram and WhatsApp.
curation.whyNotable: Backed by n8n's automation expertise, Nod combines computer-use browser automation, local-first privacy, and human-in-the-loop approval in a polished consumer-grade desktop app — a rare combination for open-source AI agents at this stage of maturity.
strengths: Local-first, privacy-preserving design with model choice flexibility
Polished cross-platform desktop experience (macOS, Windows, Linux preview) with regular releases
Human-in-the-loop safety model — asks before taking action on real websites
Strong backing from n8n with active development (45 contributors, 23 releases in 6 months) and OpenSSF Best Practices badge
limitations: Very new project (created Sept 2026) — long-term stability and feature completeness uncertain
No Docker support or headless/server deployment option limits enterprise and CI use cases
Dependent on third-party LLM providers (ChatGPT Plus/Pro or external API keys), which may introduce cost or availability constraints
useCases: Automating repetitive personal admin tasks (invoice follow-up, subscription/trial cancellation)
Privacy-conscious users who want AI assistance without sending data to cloud agents
n8n ecosystem users seeking a complementary local agent for real-world browser actions
curation.targetAudience: Individuals who want a self-hosted, privacy-respecting AI personal assistant; n8n power users; people interested in local-first AI tooling
curation.oneLiner: A local-first personal AI agent that autonomously operates real websites on your behalf — with your model, your machine, and your approval.

name: Crest
description: An open source browser for Mac, iPhone, and iPad.

curation.summary: Crest is an open-source, privacy-focused browser for macOS, iOS, and iPadOS built with SwiftUI. Its key differentiator is 'Spaces'—isolated browsing contexts with separate cookies, history, credentials, and sync identities—along with a Mac version that runs on both Chromium and WebKit engines. The project targets users who want stronger boundaries between work, personal, and private browsing.
curation.whyNotable: Crest introduces a novel 'Spaces' concept that goes beyond traditional tab groups or profiles by isolating cookies, history, credentials, and sync identity per Space, while also supporting Sub-Spaces that selectively share state. It's one of the few open-source browsers targeting Apple platforms natively with SwiftUI, filling a niche left by Safari, Chrome, and Firefox.
strengths: Innovative Spaces model providing true isolation of cookies, history, credentials, and sync identity
Native SwiftUI implementation across macOS, iOS, and iPadOS with dual-engine support (Chromium + WebKit) on Mac
Strong open-source commitment with MPL-2.0 license, CI/CD, frequent releases (100 in 6 months), and an active public roadmap
limitations: No automated test suite despite having CI
Very high open-issue count (306) relative to contributor base (21), suggesting backlog pressure
Reliance on Chromium/WebKit engines means core rendering innovation is limited; differentiation is primarily at the UX/session-management layer
useCases: Separating work, personal, and private browsing contexts with strict cookie/data isolation
Managing multiple client accounts via Sub-Spaces that share credentials but keep tabs separate
Privacy-conscious users on Apple platforms wanting an open-source alternative to commercial browsers
curation.targetAudience: Privacy-minded Apple ecosystem users, professionals juggling multiple roles or clients, and open-source software advocates on macOS/iOS/iPadOS.
curation.oneLiner: An open-source Apple-native browser that reinvents browsing isolation through independently scoped 'Spaces' with shared-subspace flexibility.

name: morphe-patches
description: Morphe Patches

curation.summary: morphe-patches is a Java-based Android patching project (part of the Morphe App ecosystem) that appears to provide modification patches for Android applications. The repository was created in late 2025 and grew extremely quickly, amassing over 5,000 stars within its first year with very high release cadence (100 releases in 6 months) and a large contributor base.
curation.whyNotable: The project's explosive growth and release velocity suggest it fills a real demand in the Android modding/patching community, likely as a ReVanced-alternative patch collection. However, the repository is essentially undocumented beyond branding assets, making it hard to assess its exact purpose and technical approach.
strengths: Extremely fast growth and community adoption (5k+ stars within ~1 year)
Very active development with high release cadence (100 releases in 6 months) and 111 contributors
Established CI pipeline and permissive-copyleft licensing (GPL-3.0)
limitations: Documentation is essentially absent — README consists almost entirely of branding/SVG logo markup, making the project's purpose and usage unclear
No test suite despite claims of production-like activity, raising reliability concerns for a code-injection tool
High ratio of open issues (532) relative to visible roadmap or contribution guidelines suggests triage strain
useCases: Patching Android applications to modify or extend their behavior
Community-driven alternatives to official Android app restrictions/features
Customizing Android client apps via reusable patch bundles
curation.targetAudience: Android power users and developers interested in app modification/patching tooling
curation.oneLiner: A fast-growing but poorly documented Android app patch collection with impressive community momentum.

curation.summary: LSPrivilege is a Kotlin-based Android kernel privilege-escalation application that obtains temporary root through pluggable exploit backends (currently CVE-2026-43499) and can load root managers such as KernelSU or APatch. It ships both a GUI app and a native CLI, with kernel profiles derived from OTA ZIPs or boot images and strict per-device offset validation.
curation.whyNotable: It is one of the more modular and professionally documented efforts in the Android rooting space, decoupling exploit payloads from root-manager loading and treating kernel support as versioned, importable profiles rather than hardcoded offsets. With ~3.3k stars, 61 contributors, CI, and regular releases, it reflects an active, community-backed approach to kernel-level privilege escalation on Android.
strengths: Modular, multi-backend architecture rather than a single hardcoded exploit, making it extensible to future CVEs
Unusually thorough documentation: bilingual README, porting guide, MediaTek address-recovery guide, and a supported-devices list
Dual delivery model: polished GUI app plus a scriptable native CLI with prebuilt/exported kernel profiles
Active maintenance with 61 contributors, CI, and recent releases
limitations: No automated tests; reliability depends heavily on manual profile validation and the uname -r match gate
Applicability is narrow and per-device, and only one exploit backend is currently shipped despite plans for more
382 open issues suggest a substantial support burden relative to maintainer capacity
useCases: Gaining temporary root and loading KernelSU/APatch-style modules on supported Android kernels
Mobile kernel security research, vulnerability reproduction, and exploit prototyping
Extracting kernel offsets and generating per-device profiles from boot images or OTA packages
curation.targetAudience: Android power users, custom-ROM maintainers, kernel developers, and mobile security researchers comfortable with low-level boot-chain concepts
curation.oneLiner: A profile-driven Android kernel privilege-escalation toolkit that turns individual CVEs into reusable, multi-manager root loaders.
